claims.text: C1 has 27.9% lower count error than one global factor, baseline (b), on the final set, 95% interval 18.6% to 30.5%, beyond noise. It also passed against the raw splice, baseline (a). Baseline (c), Aqua only, is not scored on count error.

figures.name: error reduction, C1 against (b), final set
C1 passed the test against (a), final set

claims.text: C1 failed the flag-precision test against (b): 0.704 against 0.736. Under the rule fixed beforehand the outcome was "nothing beat one global factor", and the project lead kept C1 as a recorded deviation after seeing the scores.

figures.name: precision difference C1 minus (b) is beyond noise
C1 passed the test against (b), final set

claims.text: The trade-off: on the final set C1's flags caught more of the true anomalies than (b)'s (recall 0.761 against 0.690) and were right less often. In plain words, more true alerts and more false alarms.
The final-set score is slightly optimistic because C1 is the best of three.

figures.name: lowest-error approach of the three scored on the final set

claims.text: On the final set, the region-month comparator, one factor per region and calendar month that was never eligible for the pick, passed the test against (b): 10.3% lower count error, 95% interval 4.1% to 10.8%, and higher flag precision (0.756 against 0.736). C1 has 18.4% lower count error than the comparator, 95% interval 8.2% to 22.8%, and lower flag precision (0.704 against 0.756), both beyond noise.

figures.name: comparator passed the test against (b), final set
error reduction, comparator against (b), final set
comparator minus (b) precision is beyond noise
error reduction, C1 against the comparator, final set
C1 minus the comparator precision is beyond noise

claims.text: On the final set C1 had 3.9% lower count error than 4A, 95% interval 1.7% to 5.8%, short of the margin fixed beforehand, so under that rule the simpler 4A was preferred; 4A also failed the flag-precision test against (b).

figures.name: error reduction, C1 against 4A, final set
C1's error was not lower by the margin
the single approach the margin was tested against
4A passed the test against (b), final set

claims.text: Real Aqua is the record through December 2021 because every method failed against Aqua only.
On the final set, flags in southern Africa were right less than half the time for every candidate method and both baselines: C1 0.453, 4A 0.473, 1A 0.408, (b) 0.459, (a) 0.164.
The two flag tiers were checked on selection years only.
NOAA-20 is untested against Aqua. The comparison of NOAA-20 with Suomi NPP is reported only.

Reported-only run (2012–2013, 2022–2026 and Punjab; never used for the pick), against (b): C1 has 20.2% lower count error, 95% interval 14.8% to 24.6%, and lower flag precision (0.720 against 0.738), both beyond noise. Recall is 0.695 against 0.631.

figures.name: error reduction, C1 against (b), reported-only set
precision difference C1 minus (b) is beyond noise

claims.text: On that reported-only set 4A alone passed the (b) test (12.2% lower error, precision within noise) and C1 did not. C1 has 6.5% lower error than 4A and 0.008 lower precision. This did not change the pick, because reported-only results never do.

claims.text: In southern Africa on the reported-only set, 4A did better than C1 (error 45.50 against 51.97) and C1 ran 16.8% low. In Punjab 1A did best (29.45 against C1's 31.59).
